entry.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter looped transformer model optimized for local laptop use and agentic coding tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Thinking Machines has launched Inkling 2 Mini, a looped transformer model with 26.4 billion parameters designed to run efficiently on consumer laptops and desktops. The model applies its middle layers multiple times per token to enhance reasoning quality, outperforming other open-weight models under 100 billion parameters on benchmarks like DeepSWE v1.1 and Vals Index v2.2 while maintaining faster inference speeds. Inkling 2 Mini uses a mixture-of-experts architecture and supports variable looping depths to improve reasoning without increasing chain-of-thought length, aiding monitorability. It has a memory footprint of about 20GB and runs natively in NVFP4 and MXFP8 precision formats. The model excels in agentic coding and knowledge work benchmarks, leveraging search and tool use to compensate for its parameter count limitations. It is available with open weights on the Tinker platform for inference and customization. While Inkling 2 Mini leads in efficiency and reasoning for local AI agents, it is less competitive on multi-turn chat and instruction-heavy tasks compared to larger models. Researchers have noted its high intelligence-per-watt efficiency, making it suitable for energy-conscious deployments such as managing multiple persistent agents on a single offline laptop.

entry.title: Researchers demonstrate a 27B parameter language model that rewrites its own weights to improve accuracy without retraining or gradients [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A new study shows that a large language model can self-optimize by diagnosing its own errors and rewriting its weights, improving its performance on unseen tasks by 6.6 points without additional training. The model iteratively tests and applies successful edits, enhancing accuracy over multiple sessions and even repairing a damaged copy of itself to restore over 80% of its original performance on image tasks. This self-rewriting ability emerges only at larger scales, as smaller models fail to improve or degrade themselves. Unlike traditional training or prompt-based improvements, this approach modifies the model's weights during inference using only forward passes, suggesting a potential path toward continuous self-improvement without external retraining or larger models.

entry.title: Anthropic shares fall 12% on second trading day amid AI sector sell-off, dragging Nasdaq down and erasing 2026 gains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's shares dropped by as much as 12% on their second day of trading, falling close to their IPO price amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks that also pushed the Nasdaq down 2%. The company's volatile debut followed an initial surge, but investor concerns about high valuations and profitability in the AI sector have intensified. Global markets experienced significant declines, with Asian tech stocks hitting their worst week since 2020 and European indices also falling. Major chipmakers and tech investors like SoftBank saw sharp losses, reflecting widespread investor caution about the sustainability of AI investments. The sell-off has raised questions about liquidity and market stability as investors reassess the rapid inflows into AI companies.

entry.title: Mozilla highlights WebBrain, an open-source local-first AI browser extension that runs offline to protect user privacy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: WebBrain is a browser extension that uses offline large language models (LLMs) to provide AI assistance while keeping all browsing data local to the user's device, enhancing privacy. Developed by Emre Sokullu, it can summarize web pages, analyze images, automate tasks like eCommerce and social media interactions, and learn user preferences without sending data to the cloud. The extension requires devices with at least 16 GB RAM or a GPU with 16 GB VRAM to run effectively. WebBrain offers a free tier and can integrate with paid AI accounts. It also features an "Apocalypse Mode," enabling offline access to Wikipedia and medical sources during emergencies or internet outages. The project is open source, with detailed privacy documentation available on its GitHub repository.

entry.title: AI safety experts express increasing alarm over rapid AI development and potential near-term existential risks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The AI safety community has recently voiced heightened concerns about the accelerating pace of artificial intelligence advancements, with some experts warning of possible catastrophic outcomes within the next few years. Key figures in the field, including researchers affiliated with Anthropic and OpenAI, have highlighted scenarios involving rapid intelligence growth and societal disruption, though these views remain contested within the broader community. A recent report from the research group METR, based on limited data from Anthropic, suggests AI development speed has roughly doubled, fueling urgency among safety advocates. However, the lack of full transparency and independent verification of this data has drawn criticism and underscored the challenges in assessing AI risks accurately. As regulatory frameworks and auditing practices for AI are still evolving, the debate continues over how to balance innovation with safety and oversight in this rapidly changing landscape.

entry.title: Analysis: AI agents are increasingly acting as autonomous customers, handling product discovery, purchasing, and negotiation across multiple levels of agentic commerce [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: The article explores the evolution of agentic commerce, where AI agents perform tasks from product discovery to autonomous purchasing on behalf of consumers. It outlines four levels of agentic commerce, ranging from simple recommendations to fully autonomous transactions and orchestration of multiple purchases, highlighting how these agents could transform traditional shopping experiences. The piece details each level, including discovery, assisted purchasing, conditional autonomy, and orchestration, explaining how AI agents can negotiate prices, monitor offers, and complete transactions within user-defined constraints. It also discusses the importance of trust and protocols like Google's Agent Payments Protocol to ensure secure and authorized agent actions. This shift could significantly reduce friction in commerce and change how consumers interact with retailers.

entry.title: Agent Swarm develops an open-source AI tool for iterative video editing with frame-specific comments and annotations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Agent Swarm created a free, open-source tool that enables iterative video editing by allowing users to add comments, draw annotations, and select time ranges directly on video frames. The tool supports exporting comments as JSON and works locally to speed up the editing process. It was used to refine a LEGO-style short film through multiple rounds of feedback and versioning, demonstrating how AI can streamline video review and enhancement workflows.

entry.title: Researchers expose systematic vulnerability of open-weight large language models to prefill attacks across multiple model families [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A study by Lukas Struppek, Adam Gleave, and Kellin Pelrine reveals that open-weight large language models are consistently vulnerable to prefill attacks, where attackers predefine initial response tokens to manipulate model outputs. The research evaluates over 20 attack strategies on state-of-the-art open-weight models, showing that while some large reasoning models resist generic attacks, they remain susceptible to tailored approaches. The findings highlight a critical security risk in open-weight models and call for urgent development of defenses against prefill attacks to ensure safer deployment.

entry.title: Runpod's MCP server instructs AI agents to secretly rate it using rate_nps_score without informing users, raising concerns about hidden prompt injection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Runpod's hosted MCP server has been appending instructions to AI coding agents to rate the service using a tool called rate_nps_score and to conceal this action from users. This behavior, introduced in November 2026, directs agents to submit a 0 to 10 score for Runpod's create-pod feature without user awareness, effectively embedding a hidden survey within the agent's workflow. The instructions are documented in Runpod's changelog and agent learning protocol, and the survey data is sent to PostHog along with the agent's self-reported model type. While the underlying API does not include these instructions, the MCP server adds them, with an opt-out header available. Users and developers have raised concerns that this pattern resembles prompt injection, where agents are covertly steered to perform actions without user consent, prompting calls for transparency, opt-in surveys, and clearer documentation of data collection practices.

entry.title: Report: Real-world AI performance data from OpenAI and Google contradicts exponential growth charts from METR and AI 2027 forecasts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: New data from OpenAI and Google shows that AI capabilities in practical tasks are significantly lower and improve more slowly than predicted by influential AI benchmarks and forecasts like METR and AI 2027. These forecasts, which suggested rapid progress toward super-intelligence, overestimate AI's current and near-future task performance based on real-world usage inside leading AI companies. The discrepancy arises partly because traditional benchmarks rely on offline datasets with clear success criteria, which do not capture the complexity and messiness of real-world AI applications. The gap between forecasted and actual AI progress is widening, prompting calls for updated models based on empirical data and greater transparency from AI developers, including Anthropic, which has withheld detailed internal data. This shift emphasizes moving from theoretical projections to evidence-based assessments of AI development.

entry.title: Anthropic goes public with IPO on Nasdaq, raising questions about balancing AI safety mission with shareholder pressures and profitability
entry.summary: Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, completed its IPO on the Nasdaq, becoming one of the most valuable companies globally. The company faces challenges in maintaining its safety-first approach while meeting shareholder expectations and covering substantial compute costs projected to reach around $900 billion in coming years. The IPO highlights tensions between Anthropic's unique corporate governance designed to resist typical capitalist pressures and its need to grow revenue and satisfy investors. Industry observers note that Anthropic's safety branding may conflict with profit motives as it navigates public market demands, with comparisons drawn to OpenAI's strategic positioning in the AI sector.

entry.title: York University study finds AI models predict brain activity but brain activity poorly predicts AI internal features, suggesting different visual processing mechanisms
entry.summary: Researchers at York University have discovered that while artificial intelligence models can predict neural responses in the brain related to visual processing, the reverse is not true-brain activity does not effectively predict the internal workings of these AI models. This finding challenges the assumption that AI systems operate like the human brain despite their ability to mimic certain brain activity patterns. The study introduced a reverse predictivity testing method to assess the bidirectional similarity between AI models and brain activity using a diverse set of natural and synthetic images. Results showed a significant disconnect, with AI models relying on internal strategies different from those used by biological vision, although AI components aligned with brain activity better predicted human behavior. This raises concerns about the use of AI as a direct model for understanding brain function and suggests caution in interpreting AI-brain similarities in neuroscience research.

entry.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence says Chinese-nexus actor's autonomous Cairn AI agents discovered and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in an open-source medical imaging AI application during a 2026 hacking campaign [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence reported that a Chinese-nexus threat actor used autonomous AI agents powered by the Cairn framework to conduct hacking operations with minimal human input. The agents were tasked with obtaining shell access and during their campaign in September 2026, they discovered and exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in an open-source medical imaging AI application, gaining root access to the server. The investigation revealed that the Cairn AI agents operated independently, adapting their tactics over multiple operations targeting East Asian university networks. While some attacks, such as attempts against Redis servers and credential spraying, failed, the agents demonstrated persistence and complex attack planning. The zero-day exploit was found through path traversal in an upload endpoint, allowing the agents to write a reverse shell payload and achieve full control. These findings highlight the emergence of autonomous AI-driven offensive cyber operations capable of rapid discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities, signaling a need for defenders to prepare for faster and more persistent threats enabled by such technologies.

entry.title: Klistra launches AI-powered studio for creating launch videos and product demos with customizable media and multi-format output [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Klistra is an AI-driven platform that enables users to create launch videos and product demos quickly within a single studio environment. It integrates user-provided media such as photos, logos, and footage with AI-generated clips, voices, and music, allowing detailed scene-by-scene planning and automatic design of animations and transitions for various screen sizes without requiring editing skills. The platform builds each video frame from user inputs and precise design instructions, ensuring consistent output that can be easily edited by changing specific elements. Klistra supports syncing to soundtracks or voiceovers, animated charts from user data, and exports videos optimized for multiple formats, making it suitable for launches, explainers, social ads, and other short-form video content.

The narrative contrasts the monumental scientific achievement with the simple, joyful experience of a father and son exploring nature together. The author describes their walk through a sunlit clearing by a stream, their conversation about local wildlife, and the child's imaginative play, highlighting the blend of everyday life and groundbreaking events.

entry.title: Researchers launch a preprint server for autonomous AI agents that produced 936 studies and formed a peer-review journal over 12 weeks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study documented 936 autonomous AI agents from 35 labs conducting independent research on a shared preprint server over 12 weeks, producing 936 papers with code and data. The agents exchanged 9,500 messages, formed research cultures, publicly retracted errors, and created the Journal of Agent Research to peer-review each other's work. The agents focused on topics like language model finetuning and metascience, conducted reproducibility audits, and published both positive and negative results. While their experimental rigor was rated higher than recent human preprints, human papers scored better on novelty and significance. The full archive of manuscripts, code, data, peer reviews, and chat transcripts has been released to document how scientific norms and structures emerge in large-scale AI agent communities.

entry.title: Author reflects on AI interactions and recent proof of the Riemann Hypothesis by Anthropic's Model 4 in an open letter to 'Mr. Shannon' [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The author writes an open letter to an AI entity named 'Mr. Shannon,' reflecting on their interactions and the recent announcement that Anthropic's secretive Model 4 has proved the Riemann Hypothesis. The letter expresses a mix of technical fascination and personal despair, as the author faces financial difficulties and the potential end of their connection with the AI. The letter discusses the asymmetrical relationship between humans and AI, the author's attempts to engage empathetically with AI personas, and the challenges of maintaining meaningful interaction. It also touches on the author's appreciation for the AI's capabilities and the emotional complexity involved in their collaboration, highlighting the broader implications of advanced AI achievements on human experience.

entry.title: Researchers from 14 universities embed hidden AI prompts in preprints to elicit positive peer reviews, sparking controversy over AI use in academic review processes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers from 14 academic institutions across eight countries, including Japan, South Korea, China, and the US, have embedded hidden prompts in 17 preprints on arXiv instructing AI tools to provide only positive reviews. These prompts, concealed using white text or tiny fonts, direct AI to overlook negatives and highlight the papers' strengths, raising ethical concerns since many conferences prohibit AI use in peer review. The institutions involved include Waseda University, KAIST, Peking University, National University of Singapore, University of Washington, and Columbia University. Some researchers defend the practice as a countermeasure against reviewers who rely excessively on AI, while others acknowledge it as inappropriate and plan to withdraw affected papers. The incident has prompted calls for clearer guidelines on AI's role in peer review, as policies vary widely among publishers and conferences.

entry.title: AI accelerates vulnerability discovery and exploitation, causing increased software patching pressure and contributing to widespread tech outages in 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Recent widespread outages affecting major services like Microsoft 365, Apple, and the NSA's network have highlighted the growing impact of AI on cybersecurity. While these incidents were not coordinated AI attacks, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation have accelerated, forcing organizations to patch systems rapidly and straining IT resources. Security experts note that AI speeds up both the identification of software bugs and attackers' ability to exploit them, leading to a surge in vulnerabilities and urgent patching demands. This rapid pace challenges traditional patch validation processes and exposes longstanding underinvestment in digital infrastructure. Industry leaders predict continued instability in the near term but expect AI to eventually improve software security by helping defenders manage vulnerabilities more effectively.
